articles.title: Import Royalty
articles.summary: Glowing magenta and violet vinyl slashes crossing over near-black, with bright prismatic edges like a tuner wrap. A loud neon pink, purple and blue slash graphic on black; the crossing ribbons are the whole look and read from far away as tuner-style neon streaks.
articles.what: Layered razor vinyl slashes with prismatic tuner-wrap edges. Up close: Big overlapping glossy ribbons crossing in an X on near-black violet, each ribbon a soft gradient from orange through hot pink and magenta to violet and cyan, with bright white-pink glowing edges and round-cornered cut-outs. Soft blurred borders; no fine texture, shapes are palm to arm size. From a distance: A loud neon pink, purple and blue slash graphic on black; the crossing ribbons are the whole look and read from far away as tuner-style neon streaks. Measured spec (average): metal 86, roughness 74, coat 135. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, sides.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Import Royalty" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Doors and quarters: big ribbons need long panels
Hood and roof; leave some black space around the slashes
Bright and bold; use white or black numbers on a solid plate, or heavy outlines; thin numbers vanish into the glow.
Thick white or black block numbers: solid shapes survive over the glowing ribbons
Pairs well with: gloss black, chrome, white, deep purple.
pitfalls: Not a fine texture: it is large crossing ribbons, not a repeating grain
Not a smooth gradient: ribbons have hard shapes and glowing edges
Avoid: small numbers get lost in the slashes, don't stack next to other loud neon finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 86 (pearl-level metal), roughness 74 (satin gloss), clearcoat 135 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers get lost in the slashes, don't stack next to other loud neon finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: thick white or black block numbers: solid shapes survive over the glowing ribbons; a plain black stripe or panel: contrast zone for the neon
Patterns to avoid: any other multicolour or neon pattern: overload; fine textures like carbon or hex: lose the bold ribbon look
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: increases glow and edge shine; none that add noise: shapes are big and smooth
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
